name: Idols NFT self-transfer reward double-credit
summary: IdolMain._beforeTokenTransfer settles stETH rewards twice for the same holder when the sender and the receiver are the same address. It first calls _claimEthRewards(_from), which pays balanceOf(_from) * (rewardPerGod - claimedSnapshots[_from]) and writes claimedSnapshots[_from] = rewardPerGod, and then, because the sender will hold one fewer token, executes delete claimedSnapshots[_from] whenever balanceOf(_from) == 1. It then evaluates the receiver branch, where balanceOf(_to) > 0 still holds, and calls _claimEthRewards(_to) against a snapshot that has just been zeroed, paying the whole cumulative rewardPerGod again. Calling safeTransferFrom(self, self, tokenId) in a loop therefore mints one full rewardPerGod payout per iteration while the token never leaves the caller. The onlyAllowedContracts(_to) guard, which relies on Address.isContract, does not stop it because the loop runs inside the exploit contract's constructor, when its code size is still zero.
notes: IdolMain is a plain non-upgradeable ERC721Enumerable contract. Its 24,062-byte runtime is byte-identical at its creation block and at block 21624127, immediately before the exploit, so deployment is the last executable-code change.

Exact victim depletion: the sum of every stETH Transfer log emitted with IdolMain 0x439cac149b935ae1d726569800972e1669d17094 as sender to an attacker-controlled address between blocks 21624128 and 21626433, 107.685747932188918815 stETH over 51 transactions. A further 0.114227 stETH left IdolMain to four unrelated addresses in the same window and is excluded as ordinary user claims. None of the extracted amount was the attacker's entitlement: each exploit contract received its Idol immediately beforehand, which set claimedSnapshots[contract] = rewardPerGod, so its legitimate pending reward was zero. stETH is deeply liquid and was not sold through a thin market, so it is marked at the DefiLlama stETH price for the campaign-end timestamp rather than at realised proceeds. Gas is not deducted; the attacker kept the Idol NFTs, which are not part of this measurement.

The snapshot row anchored on the attacker's thirteenth exploit transaction. The anchor here is the first one, twelve blocks earlier; the later transaction remains part of the campaign and appears in the loss transaction set.
